topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

sections.title: The Analogy: The Brain vs. The Bookshelf
sections.content: Introduce the concept that Transformers have two types of memory: Attention (contextual retrieval) and MLPs (long-term factual storage). We compare the MLP to a 'key-value memory' where weights represent ingrained knowledge.
sections.example: Comparing an attention head to a librarian looking at a desk, while the MLP is the permanent encyclopedia stored in the brain.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Vector Keys
sections.content: Explain that MLP layers act as pattern matchers. If a token vector matches a 'stored pattern' (the first weight layer), it triggers the second weight layer to output a specific 'fact vector'.
sections.example: Visualizing a lock-and-key system: A 'cat' token acts as the key that opens a specific gate in the MLP to reveal the value 'mammal'.

sections.title: Deep Dive: Rank-One Model Composition
sections.content: Use a graphical representation of the weight matrices as a sum of outer products. Explain how the MLP performs a 'write' operation during training by updating weights to store specific associations.
sections.example: Visualizing a 3D grid where the MLP layer represents a cube of knowledge; 'Paris' + 'Capital Of' = 'France' node illumination.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Pattern Retrieval
sections.content: Show the step-by-step transformation: Input Vector -> Matrix Multiplication (Pattern Detection) -> Non-linearity (Activation) -> Matrix Multiplication (Fact Projection).
sections.example: A flow chart showing a 'Robot' icon input, passing through an 'Activation Gate', and outputting the fact 'Metal' into the model's prediction space.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Distributed Nature of Facts
sections.content: Summarize that facts aren't stored in one 'cell', but are distributed across multiple neurons. This explains why LLMs are robust but sometimes hallucinate.
sections.example: An animation showing a light bulb (the fact) flickering brightly when multiple relevant neurons in the MLP layer light up simultaneously.
